title: The Calling of the Fishermen
review_status: DRAFT: retelling and wondering questions require theological and editorial review before release.

source.note: Original child-friendly retelling written for this prototype; not a quotation of any translation. See also Matthew 4:18-22 and Luke 5:1-11. This is a Gospel narrative rather than a parable.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: This is a story about something that really happened, when Jesus was walking by the sea. Let's carry the material to the table, and listen.

segments.text: One day, Jesus was walking along the shore of the Sea of Galilee.
He saw two brothers, Simon and Andrew. They were fishermen, and they were throwing their net out into the water.
Jesus said to them, "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of people."
And right away, they left their nets, and they followed him.
A little farther on, Jesus saw two more brothers, James and John. They were in their boat with their father, Zebedee, mending their nets.
Jesus called them too. And they left their father in the boat with the workers, and they went with Jesus.
And from that day on, the four friends went with Jesus, wherever he went.

wonderings: I wonder what it was like to hear Jesus say, "Come, follow me."
I wonder why the brothers left their nets so quickly.
I wonder how Zebedee felt, watching his sons go.
I wonder what it means to be a fisher of people.
I wonder where Jesus might be calling you to follow him.

steps.prompt: When you're ready, return each figure to its place in the box.

feedback.mismatch: That place is shaped for a different figure.
feedback.all_good: Each figure is resting in its place.

outro.speaker: narrator
outro.text: The material is back on the shelf. It will be here whenever you want to return to it.

journal_line: I listened to the story of the fishermen who left their nets when Jesus said, "Come, follow me."
